blocks.text: Arithmetic: `+ - * / %`. With whole numbers `/` drops the fraction (`20 / 3` is 6) and `%` gives the remainder (`20 % 3` is 2).
A comparison gives `true` or `false` (a bool): `== != < > <= >=`. The logical operators are written as words: `and`, `or`, `not`.
The bit operators (`&`, `|`, `^`, `<<`, `>>`) are evaluated **before** comparisons in Greengold, so `bits & 1 == 0` means `(bits & 1) == 0`, as you would expect. (The trap from C is not here.)

blocks.prompt: Print `true` if `n` is even and `false` if it is odd. (`n % 2 == 0`)
blocks.hint: Print the condition itself instead of `false`.

blocks.why: 5 fits into 17 three times with 2 left over; `%` gives the remainder.
